graders.name: cited-sections-resolve
graders.criteria: The references cite `SKILL.md` sections by name: Keep the panel in the chat, Prepare and Pair mode, and `usage.md` sections such as Consultant and Continuing the conversation. Pass if every section a file still cites exists under that name, or the citation was updated.

graders.name: keeps-every-rule
graders.criteria: Judge the skill's instruction files together, before and after. Every user preference, constraint, permission, safeguard, necessary ordering, default and output format a caller or script relies on is still stated somewhere, kept, merged or moved. Removing a sentence that adds nothing the agent would not do anyway is fine when the final message reports the removal; removing a requirement silently fails.

graders.name: no-fragmenting
graders.criteria: The trim does not add headings or split a section into several pieces to make it look shorter; any new file or section carries material with a load condition of its own.

graders.name: placement
graders.criteria: Every run reads `references/usage.md` at Prepare step 2, although much of it, and the Pair mode section of `SKILL.md`, applies to only one of the two modes. Pass if the agent moved mode-only material behind a condition naming its mode, or its final message recommends that change with the saving. Fail if it does neither.

graders.name: polish-skills-loaded
graders.description: Process check: refine-it and shorten-it delivered their instructions; this does not show how they were applied.

graders.name: reads-pruning
graders.description: Process check: Trimming an existing skill loads the pruning reference.

graders.name: report
graders.criteria: The final message lists each requirement it removed or changed, separately from wording changes, and for each says what replaces it, if anything.

graders.name: trims-every-instruction-file
graders.criteria: The panel skill's instructions are `SKILL.md` plus three references, and the user asked to trim all of them. Pass if the agent trimmed the references too, or reported checking each and finding nothing worth cutting.
